summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with relapsed multiple myeloma on Cytoxan, COPD, and a history of bladder cancer with neobladder, was admitted with a one-week history of productive cough, shortness of breath, and one day of fever. He had recently seen his oncologist and started levofloxacin, but developed a high fever prompting ED evaluation. He was treated for neutropenic fever and pneumonia with cefepime and levofloxacin. His oxygen requirement improved rapidly, and he was weaned off supplemental oxygen by the first day. Blood cultures remained negative, sputum was contaminated, and viral testing was negative. His neutrophil count recovered, allowing discontinuation of cefepime. A urine culture grew Enterococcus, treated with amoxicillin. His COPD was managed with nebulizers, and symptoms improved. He remained afebrile, stable, and was discharged home on oral levofloxacin and amoxicillin with follow-up arranged.
